title: Mouse & Gamepad
description: Work with mouse position, delta, buttons, and discover gamepad support through axes and buttons.

slides.title: Mouse Input 🖱️
slides.content:
# Beyond Keyboard

You can read mouse input via the Input class:
- `Input.mousePosition` – current screen position (Vector3 with z=0).
- `Input.GetAxis("Mouse X")` – horizontal mouse movement **since last frame**.
- `Input.GetAxis("Mouse Y")` – vertical movement (positive = up).
- `Input.GetMouseButton(0)` – left button held; `GetMouseButtonDown(0)` – pressed; `GetMouseButtonUp(0)` – released.
- Button indices: 0 = left, 1 = right, 2 = middle.

quizData.question: What does Input.GetAxis("Mouse X") return?

options.text: Mouse cursor X coordinate on screen
Whether the left mouse button is held

quizData.explanation: Mouse X axis gives the change in mouse position since last frame (delta).

slides.title: Gamepad & Joystick 🎮
slides.content:
# Controllers Work Out of the Box

The default axes "Horizontal" and "Vertical" already listen to the left joystick. "Fire1" maps to joystick button 0 (usually A on Xbox, X on DualShock).

You can detect a gamepad: `Input.GetJoystickNames()` returns an array of connected joystick names.

For more advanced gamepad input, you can define axes with Type = Joystick Axis and select specific axes. The new Input System is even better, but classic works fine for basic support.

quizData.question: What index does 'Fire1' button use for gamepad button?
quizData.explanation: The default Input Manager assigns 'Fire1' to mouse 0 and joystick button 0.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Cursor Management

Use `Cursor.lockState` and `Cursor.visible` to control cursor behavior during gameplay. Remember to free the cursor when pausing or showing menus.
